title: Spotlight indexing
explanation: Builds the search index after files change. Normal for a few minutes after big copies or updates.

title: Window server
explanation: Manages the windows on your screen, combines them into one picture and routes your clicks and key presses to the right app.

title: Photos analysis
explanation: Analyzes your photo library in the background for Memories, People, and search by scene or object.

title: CPU heat management
explanation: Helps manage CPU temperature by making the CPU less available to busy processes. It reacts to heat and does not cause it.

title: Time Machine backup
explanation: Creates Time Machine backups and manages their history.

title: Spotlight file scanning
explanation: Scans and indexes files for Spotlight when a disk is mounted or a file changes.

title: Software updates
explanation: The main part of macOS that runs software updates.

title: iCloud app data
explanation: Supports CloudKit, the feature that lets apps store their data in iCloud.

title: iCloud documents
explanation: Supports Documents in the Cloud, the feature that stores your documents in iCloud.

title: Background network tasks
explanation: Performs network tasks for apps that set them to run in the background.

title: Tabs and sites
explanation: Draws the pages, tabs and windows of the app. Each open tab or site often runs in its own process.

title: Graphics
explanation: Draws the app's graphics and video with the graphics chip. An app usually has one.

title: Extensions
explanation: Runs the app's extensions and plug-ins apart from the main app.

title: Helpers
explanation: Runs background jobs for the app. Its memory and CPU count toward the app.

title: Google Chrome
explanation: Google's web browser. Tabs, extensions and graphics run as separate helper processes that count toward Chrome.

title: Safari
explanation: Apple's web browser. Web pages and tabs run as separate processes that count toward Safari.

title: Slack
explanation: Team chat app. It is built like a web browser, so it runs several helper processes and can use a lot of memory.

title: Xcode
explanation: Apple's app for building software. Builds, indexing and previews can use a lot of memory and CPU.

title: Claude
explanation: The Claude chat app. It is built like a web browser, so it runs several helper processes.

title: Finder
explanation: Shows your files and folders and draws the desktop. macOS restarts it at once if it quits.

title: Spotlight search
explanation: The core of Spotlight. It answers searches from Spotlight and apps, and sends new or changed files to be indexed.

title: Spotlight file scanning
explanation: Scans and indexes files for Spotlight when a disk is mounted or a file changes.

title: Spotlight search window
explanation: Shows the Spotlight window when you press Command-Space. It finds apps, files, email, messages and more.

title: File provider sync
explanation: Connects apps that supply files, such as cloud storage apps, to macOS. It lists their files and looks up file details.

title: iCloud settings sync
explanation: Stores small pieces of app data in iCloud, such as settings, so they stay the same on all your devices.

title: iCloud Photos
explanation: Runs all iCloud Photos activity, such as uploads and downloads. Busy after you add many photos.

title: Push notifications
explanation: Keeps a connection to Apple's push service, so apps and macOS get notifications and updates as soon as they are sent.

title: Photos library
explanation: Handles all requests to your Photos library, from the Photos app and from other apps.

title: Certificate checks
explanation: Checks security certificates, for example of websites and servers, to decide if they can be trusted. It does this for all apps.

title: Security policy
explanation: Decides if software may be installed, loaded or run on your Mac. Other parts of macOS ask it before they allow an action.

title: Code integrity checks
explanation: Checks the integrity of the programs that run on your Mac.

title: Malware protection
explanation: Part of XProtect, which finds and blocks known malware before it runs.

title: Keychain security
explanation: Handles keychain access and encryption tasks. It keeps private keys away from apps and checks who may use each item.

title: Keychain access
explanation: Controls who can read and change the items in your keychain, such as saved passwords.

title: App security setup
explanation: Sets up the security rules for each program when it starts.

title: App sandbox
explanation: Supports the sandbox, which limits what apps can reach. It records when an app tries to go past its limits.

title: Identity prompts
explanation: Shows the prompts that ask you to confirm it is you, and keeps track of those approvals.

title: Touch ID
explanation: Supports biometric checks, such as Touch ID fingerprint checks on Macs that have it.

title: Smart cards
explanation: Runs smart card support. It loads card drivers and keeps card sessions open.

title: User accounts
explanation: Looks up user accounts and checks passwords, on your Mac or on a directory server at work or school.

title: Firewall
explanation: Runs the macOS firewall when it is turned on. It allows or blocks incoming connections for each app.

title: Driver loader
explanation: Loads drivers (kernel extensions) into the core of macOS and starts driver extensions, when they are needed.

title: Network name lookup
explanation: Turns names, such as website addresses, into network addresses. It also finds devices such as printers on your local network.

title: System setup tracker
explanation: Keeps track of the current system setup, such as the network, and tells apps when it changes.

title: Wi-Fi
explanation: Manages your Mac's Wi-Fi hardware.

title: Wi-Fi helper
explanation: Does Wi-Fi tasks for the logged-in user, on behalf of the main Wi-Fi process.

title: Direct Wi-Fi links
explanation: Sets up direct Wi-Fi links between your Mac and nearby devices, without a Wi-Fi network in between.

title: Network add-ons
explanation: Runs network add-ons from apps, such as VPNs and content filters.

title: VPN sessions
explanation: Starts and stops VPN and content filter sessions, and sets up their network rules.

title: Device-to-device link
explanation: Lets your Apple devices talk to each other, for features such as phone call handoff.

title: AirDrop and Handoff
explanation: Runs AirDrop, Handoff, Instant Hotspot and connections to shared computers. Busy while you send or receive files with AirDrop.

title: iPhone and iPad link
explanation: Handles the connection between your Mac and an iPhone or iPad, over USB or Wi-Fi.

title: Screen Sharing
explanation: Accepts Screen Sharing connections from other computers. It runs only when Screen Sharing or Remote Management is on.

title: Sound
explanation: Part of Core Audio, the macOS sound system. It handles sound for apps, speakers, headphones and microphones.

title: Audio routing
explanation: Decides where sound plays, together with nearby Apple devices such as iPhone and iPad.

title: Bluetooth
explanation: Runs Bluetooth, which connects your Mac to devices such as keyboards, mice, trackpads, game controllers and headphones.

title: Bluetooth Low Energy
explanation: Handles Bluetooth Low Energy features. This is the power-saving kind of Bluetooth that many small accessories use.

title: Dock
explanation: Shows the Dock, where you open apps and switch between them.

title: Control Center
explanation: Shows Control Center and the system controls in the menu bar, such as Wi-Fi, sound and battery.

title: Menu bar items
explanation: Shows status items on the right side of the menu bar.

title: Login window
explanation: Shows the login window. It also keeps running while you are logged in.

title: Night Shift
explanation: Manages Night Shift, which makes the screen colors warmer at night.

title: Fonts
explanation: Makes the fonts on your Mac available to apps.

title: Icon storage
explanation: Manages the shared store of app and file icons, so icons show up quickly.

title: Screenshot tools
explanation: Shows the controls and previews when you take a screenshot or record the screen.

title: Input devices
explanation: Handles input devices, such as keyboards, mice and trackpads.

title: Accessibility
explanation: Runs accessibility services, the features that make your Mac easier to see, hear and use.

title: Universal Control
explanation: Lets you use one keyboard and mouse across your Mac and a nearby iPad or Mac.

title: Clipboard
explanation: Runs the clipboard, which holds what you copy and paste.

title: System alerts
explanation: Shows alerts from the core of macOS, such as a full disk or a file server that stopped responding.

title: Software installer
explanation: Installs software packages. Busy while an app or update installs.

title: System installer
explanation: Installs software packages for the system. Busy while an update installs.

title: App Store helper
explanation: Does background work for the App Store, such as app downloads and updates.

title: Time Machine scheduler
explanation: Decides when to start Time Machine backups and starts them.

title: Siri
explanation: Runs Siri features in the background.

title: Shortcuts
explanation: Runs and syncs the shortcuts you make in the Shortcuts app.

title: App actions
explanation: Lets Siri and Shortcuts use the actions that apps offer.

title: Suggestions
explanation: Reads content from Mail, Messages and other apps on your Mac to suggest contacts, events and words as you type.

title: AI models
explanation: Manages the AI models built into macOS and runs them when a feature needs one.

title: Notifications
explanation: Delivers notifications from apps and macOS to Notification Center.

title: System messages
explanation: Passes short status messages between programs in macOS.

title: App messages
explanation: Passes notices between apps and programs, so they can react to changes.

title: Location Services
explanation: Finds your Mac's location and controls which apps, widgets and system services may use it.

title: Significant places
explanation: Learns the places you often visit, to predict future visits.

title: System log
explanation: Collects and stores the log messages that apps and macOS write.

title: Older system log
explanation: Receives and saves log messages sent with older logging methods.

title: Live log feed
explanation: Sends live log data to Console and the log command. Uses more CPU while one of them shows a live log.

title: Crash reports
explanation: Saves a crash report when an app or process crashes. It starts on its own after each crash.

title: Hang reports
explanation: Makes a report when you force quit an app that stopped responding.

title: Analytics
explanation: Collects diagnostics and usage data on your Mac, only if you chose to share it.

title: Diagnostics upload
explanation: Sends recent diagnostic data to Apple if you chose to share it, and deletes old data that is no longer needed.

title: System monitor
explanation: Collects process data for system monitor tools.

title: Process launcher
explanation: The first process on your Mac. It starts and manages other processes and services, for the system and for each user.

title: Service starter
explanation: Prepares the setup for a helper service and then becomes that service. You see it only for a moment.

title: System event handler
explanation: Handles system events with plug-ins built into macOS.

title: App state manager
explanation: Keeps apps and processes in the right state, such as running or paused, while they have work to finish.

title: Plug-in manager
explanation: Manages and supervises the plug-ins and extensions that apps add to macOS.

title: Running apps tracker
explanation: Keeps track of the apps that are running on your Mac.

title: Settings storage
explanation: Reads and saves the settings of apps and macOS for every program that asks.

title: App automation
explanation: Passes Apple events between apps. Scripts and automation tools use them to control apps.

title: Free space manager
explanation: Watches free disk space. When space runs low, it asks apps to remove data that can be deleted, such as caches.

title: Disk housekeeping
explanation: Looks after your Mac's disks. It handles disk encryption, keeps files in order and does other housekeeping.

title: Disk manager
explanation: Notices when disks appear, tells apps about them, and makes them ready to use.

title: Document versions
explanation: Stores earlier versions of your documents, so apps can show and restore them.

title: Recent items
explanation: Keeps lists of recent and favorite files, apps and disks, such as Recent Items and part of the Finder sidebar.

title: Power management
explanation: Manages energy settings, such as when your Mac and display go to sleep.

title: System health check
explanation: Checks that macOS keeps working. If the system stops making progress, it can restart it to recover.

title: Clock sync
explanation: Keeps your Mac's clock correct by comparing it with time servers.

title: Find My Mac
explanation: Runs Find My Mac.

title: Contacts
explanation: Manages your contacts database for apps and does maintenance on it in the background.

title: Calendar data
explanation: Controls access to your calendar data and posts calendar alerts.

title: Notification Center
explanation: Shows notifications on your screen and in Notification Center.

title: Mail
explanation: Apple's email app. It can be busy for a while after you add an account, while it downloads your mail.

title: Messages
explanation: Apple's app for iMessage and text messages. It can be busy while it downloads old messages from iCloud.

title: FaceTime
explanation: Apple's app for video and audio calls. Calls use the camera, microphone and network, so CPU use rises during a call.

title: Photos
explanation: Apple's photo library app. Imports and edits can use a lot of memory. Library analysis runs in separate processes.

title: Music
explanation: Apple's app for your music library and Apple Music. Downloads and library sync use the network and disk.

title: TV
explanation: Apple's app for TV shows and movies. Video playback uses the graphics chip.

title: Notes
explanation: Apple's notes app. It syncs your notes with iCloud and your other accounts.

title: Calendar
explanation: Apple's calendar app. It syncs your events with your accounts.

title: Maps
explanation: Apple's map app. Map views, especially 3D views, use the graphics chip and the network.

title: Preview
explanation: Apple's app to view and mark up PDFs and images. Large PDFs and many open images use more memory.

title: Terminal
explanation: Apple's command-line app. Programs that you start in it count toward Terminal.

title: Activity Monitor
explanation: Apple's app that shows what each process uses.

title: System Settings
explanation: The app where you change the settings of your Mac.

title: App Store
explanation: Apple's store for apps. Downloads and updates use the network and disk.

title: Pages
explanation: Apple's app for documents and page layouts.

title: Numbers
explanation: Apple's spreadsheet app. Very large sheets and charts use more memory.

title: Keynote
explanation: Apple's presentation app. Videos and effects in slides use the graphics chip.

title: Simulator
explanation: Runs simulated iPhones, iPads and other devices to test apps. Each running device adds its own processes and memory.

title: Final Cut Pro
explanation: Apple's video editor. Rendering and exporting video can use most of the CPU and graphics chip for a long time.

title: Console
explanation: Apple's app to view logs and reports. A live log stream makes the system log work harder while it is open.

title: iPhone Mirroring
explanation: Shows and controls your iPhone on your Mac. It streams the iPhone screen, so it uses the network and graphics.

title: Brave
explanation: Brave's web browser. Tabs, extensions and graphics run as separate helper processes that count toward Brave.

title: Firefox
explanation: Mozilla's web browser. Tabs, add-ons and media run in separate processes that count toward Firefox.

title: Microsoft Edge
explanation: Microsoft's web browser. Tabs, extensions and graphics run as separate helper processes that count toward Edge.

title: Arc
explanation: The Browser Company's web browser. Tabs, extensions and graphics run as separate helper processes that count toward Arc.

title: Opera
explanation: Opera's web browser. Tabs, extensions and graphics run as separate helper processes that count toward Opera.

title: Discord
explanation: Chat app for voice, video and text. It is built like a web browser, so it runs several helper processes.

title: Microsoft Teams
explanation: Microsoft's app for chat and meetings. Video calls and screen sharing use a lot of CPU and memory.

title: Zoom
explanation: Video meeting app. Calls with video, effects or screen sharing use a lot of CPU and graphics.

title: WhatsApp
explanation: Chat and calling app. Calls and media downloads use more CPU and network.

title: Telegram
explanation: Chat app. Media downloads and large chats can use more memory and network.

title: Signal
explanation: Private chat and calling app. It is built like a web browser, so it runs several helper processes.

title: Visual Studio Code
explanation: Microsoft's code editor. It is built like a web browser. Extensions run in separate helper processes and can use a lot of CPU.

title: Cursor
explanation: AI code editor based on Visual Studio Code. Extensions and code indexing run in helper processes that count toward Cursor.

title: Zed
explanation: A fast code editor. Language tools for your projects run as separate processes and can use a lot of memory.

title: IntelliJ IDEA
explanation: JetBrains' app for building software in Java and Kotlin. Indexing a project after you open it can use a lot of CPU and memory.

title: PyCharm
explanation: JetBrains' app for building software in Python. Indexing a project after you open it can use a lot of CPU and memory.

title: Android Studio
explanation: Google's app for building Android apps. Builds, indexing and the Android emulator can use a lot of CPU and memory.

title: iTerm2
explanation: A command-line app. Programs that you start in it count toward iTerm2.

title: Warp
explanation: A command-line app with AI features. Programs that you start in it count toward Warp.

title: Ghostty
explanation: A command-line app. Programs that you start in it count toward Ghostty.

title: ChatGPT
explanation: OpenAI's ChatGPT app. It runs several helper processes that count toward ChatGPT.

title: Ollama
explanation: Runs AI models on your Mac. A model uses a lot of memory, and CPU or graphics, while it answers.

title: Notion
explanation: Notes and workspace app. It is built like a web browser, so it runs several helper processes.

title: Obsidian
explanation: Notes app that keeps your notes as plain files. It is built like a web browser, so it runs several helper processes.

title: Figma
explanation: Design app. Large design files use a lot of memory and graphics.

title: Microsoft Word
explanation: Microsoft's word processor.

title: Microsoft Excel
explanation: Microsoft's spreadsheet app. Large sheets and many formulas use more CPU and memory.

title: Microsoft PowerPoint
explanation: Microsoft's presentation app.

title: Microsoft Outlook
explanation: Microsoft's email and calendar app. It can be busy while it downloads and syncs mail.

title: 1Password
explanation: Password manager app. It is built like a web browser, so it runs several helper processes.

title: Dropbox
explanation: Syncs files with Dropbox. Busy while many files upload or download.

title: Google Drive
explanation: Syncs files with Google Drive. Busy while many files upload or download.

title: OneDrive
explanation: Syncs files with Microsoft OneDrive. Busy while many files upload or download.

title: Spotify
explanation: Music app. It is built like a web browser, so it runs several helper processes.

title: Docker Desktop
explanation: Runs software containers for developers in a hidden Linux system. That system holds its memory for as long as Docker runs.

title: Notifications
explanation: Shows the app's notifications.

title: Windows and pages
explanation: Draws the app's windows and pages. Apps built like a web browser run one or more of these.

title: Crash reporter
explanation: Watches the app and saves a crash report if the app crashes.

title: Web pages
explanation: Shows the content of a web page or tab. Busy pages, videos and many open tabs use more memory.

title: Web network
explanation: Loads web pages and files from the network for the app.

title: Web graphics
explanation: Draws web graphics and plays video and audio for the app's web pages.

title: Tabs and add-ons
explanation: Runs Firefox tabs, add-ons, graphics and media in separate processes.

title: Code completion
explanation: Gives Xcode code completion, highlighting and quick help for Swift. Busy after you open a large project.

title: Builds
explanation: Runs builds for Xcode. Busy while a build runs.

title: Builds
explanation: Runs builds for Xcode. Busy while a build runs.

title: Swift compiler
explanation: Compiles Swift code during builds and previews. Many copies can run at the same time during a build.

title: Debugger
explanation: Runs the debugger while you debug an app from Xcode.

title: Previews
explanation: Runs live previews of your app's screens in Xcode.

title: Simulated device
explanation: Starts and runs the parts of a simulated device. Each running simulator has one.

title: Simulator service
explanation: Manages the simulated devices for Xcode and Simulator.

title: Media analysis
explanation: Part of macOS. Analyzes photos and videos on this Mac in the background, for example for search in Photos.

title: ChatGPT Classic
explanation: OpenAI's ChatGPT app. It runs several helper processes that count toward ChatGPT.

title: IntelliJ IDEA CE
explanation: JetBrains' app for building software in Java and Kotlin. Indexing a project after you open it can use a lot of CPU and memory.

title: PyCharm CE
explanation: JetBrains' app for building software in Python. Indexing a project after you open it can use a lot of CPU and memory.
